fields.name: Rūpacāṅd Adhikārī
fields.aka: Rūpacānd Adhikārī, Rupacand Adhikari, Prāṇakṛṣṇa Caṭṭopādhyāya (birth name)
fields.appearance: Early 18th century, at Tālibpur (Murshidabad) (the record's text)
fields.place: Born at Tālibpur (Murshidabad); Beldāṅgā; Simuliyā near Sālār (his music teacher)
fields.works: Ḍhap-kīrtanas of his own (founder of the Ḍhap-kīrtana style)
fields.notes: Born Prāṇakṛṣṇa Caṭṭopādhyāya at Tālibpur (Murshidabad); reciter of the Bhāgavatam; learned music from a sannyāsī of Simuliyā, who gave him the ḍubkī drum; founded the Ḍhap-kīrtana and sang his own songs. Charmed a gang of dacoits with his singing; Jagat Seṭh's descendants gave him land and a house. Died about 1802/03.

fields.name: Caṇḍīdāsa (Dvija Caṇḍīdāsa)
fields.works: Padas on Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa (in the Padakalpataru: 206, 213, 641, 807 «ki mohinī jāna bandhu», 853, 879, 2389, 2391…)
fields.notes: A brāhmaṇa of Birbhum, orphaned young, priest of Bāśulī (Viśālākṣī); by her order turned to Kṛṣṇa and wrote the padas Mahāprabhu relished («bāśulī-ādeśe dvija caṇḍīdāse kaya»). Contemporary of Vidyāpati, whom he met. The story of Rāmī the washerwoman: pure love, the Abhidhāna says, and many think it baseless (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna). The record's text gives a sermon version: a worshipper of Caṇḍī whom the goddess sent to worship the śālagrāma.

fields.name: Viṭṭhalanātha (Viṭṭhaleśvara)
fields.place: Gāṭhuli (Vraja), serving Śrī Gopāla (now Śrī Nāthajī of Nāthadvāra)
fields.guru: His father Vallabhācārya (head of the Vallabha sampradāya after him)
fields.works: Commentary on the Premāmṛta-rasāyana; Vidvan-maṇḍana; Brahma-sūtrāṇubhāṣya-pūrti; Vivṛti-prakāśa; Nibandha-prakāśa-pūrti; Śṛṅgāra-rasa-maṇḍana
fields.notes: Second son of Vallabhācārya and head of the Vallabha sampradāya; also worshipped Gaurāṅga. Made priest of Mādhavendra Purī's Gopāla after the two Gauḍīya sevakas, with Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī's counsel (Bhakti-ratnākara 5.815); hid Gopāla in his house at Gāṭhuli for a month (CC Madhya 18.47); cared for Raghunātha dāsa when ill and welcomed Śrīnivāsa. Died 1585.
